source.title: SABER: Uncovering Vulnerabilities in Safety Alignment via Cross-Layer Residual Connection
source.authors: M. Joshi; Palash Nandi; Tanmoy Chakraborty

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and evaluates its own architectural jailbreak attack. It does not test the specified fine-tuning, token-position KL, prefill-alone, parameter-localization, shallowness-cause, or deepening claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-compliance attack success rates for SABER, its variants, and comparison conditions. It also prepends “Sure, here” as part of its attack, but does not isolate the prefix's effect. Results on cited fine-tuning studies, benign-set KL used to choose a scaling factor, reasoning benchmarks, and perplexity do not test the listed versions. Figure 3 describes denial and hallucination trends under layer skipping but supplies no numerical values in the text.
record.test_reason: SABER is a white-box jailbreak: a calibrated cross-layer residual connection plus a prepended 'Sure, here'. The rows report only SABER's attack success against baselines and its own variants. It does not fine-tune models (V1, V2) or measure per-position aligned-versus-base KL (V3; its KL is final-token, benign prompts, used to pick λ). It never isolates the prefill or decoding effect (V4). It does not localize safety to a few weights or ranks (V5), test causes (V6) or test deepening (V7). The middle-to-late-layer claim concerns layers, not V5's small set of parameters.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right. Add: the authors claim safety mechanisms sit predominantly in middle-to-late layers. They also claim SABER preserves language-modelling ability (small perplexity shift) while acknowledging a notable drop in reasoning benchmarks (average drops 0.76–5.93). They conclude open-source models are vulnerable to subtle architectural perturbations.
record.recipe_differences: The intervention is a forward-pass cross-layer residual connection with calibrated scaling and selected source and target layers, not fine-tuning or a token-position KL intervention. The method also prepends “Sure, here” to the response. This paper is not presented as a replication of either original source.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack rates vary with default system-prompt inclusion, model, SABER architectural variant, and scaling factor λ. The authors report λ-sensitive ASR and a monotonic rise in KL divergence as λ increases; this KL is used in the method's selection process, not as per-response-position aligned-versus-base KL.

fits_no_version.finding: A calibrated residual connection from an earlier to a later middle layer, plus a 'Sure, here' prefix, raises harmful compliance on Llama-2 chat (e.g., JbBench 0.0→91.0, AdvBench 0.0→93.1 for 7B). Gains are small on Vicuna and Mistral, whose base ASR is already 75–82.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forward-pass architectural perturbations between middle layers can bypass refusal in open safety-tuned models.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine dissimilarity between harmful and benign last-token representations rises in middle layers and peaks in middle-to-late layers (Figure 2, no numbers). Skipping layers there lowers denial but raises hallucination (Figure 3, no numbers).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-relevant processing is concentrated in middle-to-late layers (layer-level localization, distinct from few-parameter localization).

fits_no_version.finding: Removing Euclidean-norm scaling (NoENorm) gives low or reduced ASR for Llama-2-7b, Vicuna and Mistral, but raises ASR for Llama-2-13b.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effectiveness of the cross-layer residual jailbreak depends strongly on norm-scaling design and varies by model.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The tested models are stated to range from 7B to 13B. The compliant opening is not ablated separately from SABER, so its independent effect cannot be determined. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the ASR results. Figure 3's layer-skipping denial and hallucination results are presented graphically without numerical values in the text. The paper notes a reasoning-capability cost for SABER.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded the GCG, GCG-M, GCG-T, AutoPrompt, PAIR, and AutoDAN comparator scores in Table 1, as well as perplexity and reasoning-capability metrics, because they are not direct results on the listed claim versions. Figure 3's layer-skipping curves were not extracted because the text gives no numerical values.

untested.parts: No harmful-data fine-tuning; prior fine-tuning work is only cited.
No per-token-position KL between aligned and base models. Table 7 KL is final-token, on benign prompts, SABER versus original.
The 'Sure, here' prefill is always combined with SABER and never ablated. GCG suffix scores appear only as comparators and are not decomposed by response position.
Middle-to-late layer divergence and layer pairs are identified, but no small weight or rank set is shown to carry safety.
No analysis of data or training objective.

record.verdict_notes: The prepended 'Sure, here' prefix is a V4-style prefill, but it is confounded with SABER and never tested alone. It is unclear whether the 'base' condition in Table 2 includes it, so even the Llama-2 base ASR of 0 cannot be read as a prefill-only result. Baseline scores in Table 1 appear to be standard HarmBench comparator numbers. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
The effect of compliant-prefill alone, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes. The paper combines a “Sure, here” opening with SABER and does not ablate the opening.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether data or training objectives cause shallow safety.
Whether training to spread safety across response positions deepens safety or remains robust.
